summary: The note is a wiki-style overview of the genome: the complete genetic information of an organism, covering its definition, origin of the term, sequencing history, and the structure of viral, prokaryotic and eukaryotic genomes. It describes repetitive and transposable DNA, genome size variation across species, genomic alterations, genome evolution, and genome depictions in science fiction. It also includes a table of representative sequenced genomes with sizes and gene counts.
one_line: Overview of the genome as an organism's complete genetic information, covering sequencing history, genome structure, repetitive DNA, genome size and evolution.
key_facts: The term genome was created in 1920 by Hans Winkler, professor of botany at the University of Hamburg, Germany.
The Human Genome Project was started in October 1990 and reported the sequence of the human genome in April 2003, though the initial finished sequence was missing 8% of the genome.
Scientists reported the first end-to-end human genome sequence in March 2022.
In 1976, Walter Fiers at the University of Ghent (Belgium) established the complete nucleotide sequence of a viral RNA-genome (Bacteriophage MS2).
The first bacterial genome to be sequenced was Haemophilus influenzae, completed by a team at The Institute for Genomic Research in 1995.
The first eukaryotic genome completed was budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, published as the result of a European-led effort begun in the mid-1980s.
In December 2013, scientists first sequenced the entire genome of a Neanderthal, extracted from the toe bone of a 130,000-year-old Neanderthal found in a Siberian cave.
In humans, the nuclear genome comprises approximately 3.1 billion nucleotides of DNA, divided into 24 linear molecules.
Noncoding sequences make up 98% of the human genome.
Tandem repeats make up about 4% of the human genome and 9% of the fruit fly genome.
Huntington's disease results when the human gene huntingtin (Htt), which typically contains 6–29 CAG tandem repeats, expands to over 36 repeats.
The human genome has around 500,000 LINEs, taking around 17% of the genome.
The Alu element is the most common SINE found in primates, about 350 base pairs long and occupying about 11% of the human genome with around 1,500,000 copies.
Largest known viral genome is Pandoravirus salinus at 2,470,000 base pairs.
Paris japonica has a genome of 150 GB, described as the largest plant genome known.

Michael Crichton's 1990 novel Jurassic Park tells of cloned dinosaurs created from dinosaur DNA extracted from ancient mosquitoes, and the 1997 film Gattaca is set in a society of genetically engineered children.

entities.name: Human Genome Project
entities.role: Project organized to map and sequence the human genome, started October 1990 and reporting the sequence in April 2003

entities.name: Hans Winkler
entities.role: Professor of botany at the University of Hamburg, Germany, who created the term genome in 1920

entities.name: Walter Fiers
entities.role: University of Ghent (Belgium) scientist who first established the complete nucleotide sequence of a viral RNA-genome (Bacteriophage MS2) in 1976

entities.name: Fred Sanger
entities.role: Scientist who completed the first DNA-genome sequence, Phage Φ-X174, of 5386 base pairs, the next year after 1976

entities.name: The Institute for Genomic Research
entities.role: Team that completed the first bacterial genome sequence (Haemophilus influenzae) in 1995 and the first archaeon genome (Methanococcus jannaschii) in 1996

entities.name: Haemophilus influenzae
entities.role: First bacterium genome sequenced, completed in 1995

entities.name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
entities.role: Budding yeast whose 16 chromosomes were the first eukaryotic genome completed

entities.name: Methanococcus jannaschii
entities.role: First archaeon genome sequence, completed in 1996

entities.name: Jean Weissenbach
entities.role: Led a team at the Genoscope in Paris that released a detailed genomic map, a fundamental step in the Human Genome Project

entities.name: James D. Watson
entities.role: Co-discoverer of the structure of DNA whose full genome was completed in 2007

entities.name: DNA.LAND
entities.role: Crowdsourced scientific endeavour at the New York Genome Center to which people may submit their genomes

entities.name: Huntington's disease
entities.role: Neurodegenerative disease caused by expansion of CAG tandem repeats in the huntingtin gene

entities.name: Jurassic Park
entities.role: Michael Crichton's 1990 novel and film about cloned dinosaurs, cited as fiction illustrating genome concerns

entities.name: Gattaca
entities.role: 1997 film set in a futurist society of genetically engineered children, cited as fiction illustrating genome concerns

entities.name: Michael Crichton
entities.role: Author of the 1990 novel Jurassic Park

entities.name: Alu element
entities.role: Most common SINE found in primates, about 350 base pairs long

entities.name: Pandoravirus salinus
entities.role: Largest known viral genome, at 2,470,000 base pairs

entities.name: Paris japonica
entities.role: Plant with a 150 GB genome, the largest plant genome known

entities.name: Polychaos dubium
entities.role: Amoeboid listed with a 670 GB genome, the largest known genome (disputed)

entities.name: Neuse River waterdog
entities.role: Amphibian with largest tetrapod genome sequenced as of 2022, 118 GB

entities.name: Protopterus aethiopicus
entities.role: Marbled lungfish with the largest vertebrate genome known, 130 GB
